assignments.reason: Complete faith (אמונה שלמה) is the perfected state of אמונה itself — it is faith at its fullest. Its essential nature IS faith. It appears in edge 1015 where complete faith CAUSES eating to be permitted, but the concept itself belongs to the faith domain. The Torah states (line 15): 'כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אֱמוּנָה בִּשְׁלֵמוּת, יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילָתוֹ יִחוּד' — faith in completeness is the prerequisite.

The completion and adornment of faith (שלמות וקשוטי אמונה) is an attribute of faith itself — it describes faith in its adorned, perfected state. The additions file already identifies קשוטי אמונה as belonging to Package 1. The concept IS faith (in its adorned form), not something produced by faith. Line 16: 'וְעִקַּר שְׁלֵמוּת וְקִשּׁוּטֵי אֱמוּנָה, הַיְנוּ לְקָרֵב דַּוְקָא הַמְרֻחָקִים.'

Drawing close the distant ones (לקרב דוקא המרחקים) is identified in the additions file as the bechina equivalent of קשוטי אמונה — it IS the adornment of faith. Its essential nature is the outreach dimension of faith: the Torah says faith is completed/adorned when the far-away come near (line 16). This concept belongs to the faith domain because it IS what faith looks like when perfected — the concept is inherently about faith's completion, not a separate domain.

The purification/clarification of foods (והברור של המאכלים) is the spiritual process of separating good from evil in food before eating. In edge 298, this purification is CAUSED BY faith. However, its essential nature is the positive process of birur — clarification, purification, which is the constructive/holy preparatory act. It is the practical instrument that enables holy eating, parallel in function to fasting (both are purifying practices). The Torah states (line 3-4): 'הָאֲכִילָה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת מַאֲכָל אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר... וְהַבֵּרוּר שֶׁל הַמַּאֲכָלִים הוּא עַל יְדֵי אֱמוּנָה.' The birur is the positive, constructive holy process — same domain as faith and fasting.

Cleaving to the back of holiness (דבקות אחורי הקדשה) is the mystical mechanism by which fasting works — it seals the back of holiness so the klipot cannot suckle. Its essential nature is a holy protective practice: the word 'דבקות' (cleaving) and 'קדושה' (holiness) place it firmly in the holy domain. In edge 707, fasting CAUSES this cleaving; the cleaving itself IS a holy state. Line 23: 'וּדְבֵקוּת אֲחוֹרֵי הַקְּדֻשָּׁה, הִיא עַל יְדֵי הַתַּעֲנִית.' It is the mechanism of fasting, belonging to the same constructive/holy domain as Package 1.

assignments.node_id: הוא ממשיך מימי החסדים ללחלח הגרון, ואז יוכל לדבר.
assignments.reason: Drawing down waters of kindness to moisten the throat so one can speak — this describes the positive healing result of fasting upon speech. Its essential nature is a healing/restorative holy process: חסדים (kindnesses) moistening the constricted throat. In edge 812 fasting CAUSES this, but the concept itself is the divine kindness flowing to heal. Line 26: 'וְעַל יְדֵי הַתַּעֲנִית שֶׁמַּרְעִיב אֶת עַצְמוֹ, הוּא מַמְשִׁיךְ מֵימֵי הַחֲסָדִים לְלַחְלֵח הַגָּרוֹן.' The concept of 'waters of kindness moistening the throat' is a holy restorative state belonging to the constructive/positive domain of Package 1.

Raising the sparks of speech (להעלות ניצוצי הדבור) is the holy act of elevating fallen holy sparks from among the klipot back to holiness. Its essential nature is tikkun — rectification, restoration of holiness. In edge 1595, fasting CAUSES this elevation. But the concept itself IS a holy restorative process: the word 'להעלות' (to raise up) and 'ניצוצי' (sparks of holiness) place it in the constructive domain. Line 17: 'צָרִיךְ מִתְּחִלָּה לְהַעֲלוֹת נִיצוֹצֵי אוֹתִיּוֹת הַדִּבּוּר.' It is the positive purpose that fasting serves.

new_packages.label: אֲכִילָה קְדוֹשָׁה וְיִחוּד
new_packages.reason: Torah #62 opens and closes with the thesis that the eating of Israel produces the unification (yichud) of the Holy One and the Shekhinah face to face. The concepts of eating (אכילה), the yichud it produces, and the permitting of eating (התרה אכילה) form a coherent thematic cluster that is distinct from faith (Package 1) and fasting (also Package 1). While faith and fasting are the INSTRUMENTS that enable holy eating, eating and its cosmic result (yichud) constitute the GOAL and OUTCOME domain. These nodes are not faith-concepts or fasting-concepts by nature; they are eating-and-unification concepts. The Torah explicitly opens (line 2): 'עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילָתָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל נַעֲשֶׂה יִחוּד קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּהּ אַפִּין בְּאַפִּין' and closes (line 50): 'עַל יְדֵי אֱמוּנָה בִּשְׁלֵמוּת, אֲזַי הֻתְּרָה אֲכִילָה, בְּחִינַת וַיַּסֵּב.' The eating-yichud pair is the Torah's central thesis.

new_packages.label_en: Torah Study and Peace — Study of Legal Decisors
new_packages.reason: The Torah dedicates a significant structural section (lines 10-14, 51-54) to the causal chain: study of legal decisors (פוסקים) → peace in holiness (שלום שבקדושה) → resolution of the evil-inclination's division in the heart → ability to serve God with both inclinations → knowing how to answer heresy. These nodes form a coherent cluster about TORAH STUDY AS PEACE-MAKING. Their essential nature is the domain of Torah learning (specifically halachic decisors) and its product of peace/resolution. This is distinct from faith (Package 1) and from fasting (also Package 1) — it is the domain of intellectual Torah study that resolves the dispute. The Torah explicitly states (line 12): 'וְתִקּוּן הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁבִּקְדֻשָּׁה, הֵן הֲלָכוֹת פְּסוּקוֹת. כִּי פְּסַק הֲלָכָה הוּא הַשָּׁלוֹם וְהַכְרָעָה.'

new_packages.label: דִּבּוּר
new_packages.reason: Speech (דבור) is a central structural concept in Torah #62: the purification of speech is the means by which the sparks are gathered from the klipot, which causes the nations to abandon idolatry and embrace Israel's faith (lines 17-18). Speech is not faith, not fasting, not eating — it is a distinct domain. The Torah describes speech as having its own exile (גלות מצרים = מצר הגרון) and its own restoration (through fasting → moistening the throat → speech returns). The dibbur acts as its own agent: 'הוֹפֵךְ אֶת עַצְמוֹ הַדִּבּוּר, וּמְלַקֵּט הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת הַקְּדֻשָּׁה מִבֵּין הַקְּלִפּוֹת' (line 17). Speech is the active instrument of tikun in this Torah.

unassigned_nodes.reason: This is a compound conditional statement ('if a person knew with a complete heart that the whole earth is filled with His glory and God stands during prayer and hears prayer') rather than a single concept. It describes a hypothetical state of complete knowledge. Its nature spans knowledge (yedia), heart-wholeness (lev shalem), prayer (tefillah), and divine omnipresence — multiple domains at once. It does not fit neatly into any single existing package: it is not faith per se (it describes KNOWLEDGE, not faith), not fasting, not desires. It could partially relate to the new Torah/Shalom package (since knowledge/intellect is involved) but the prayer dimension and the heart-wholeness dimension pull it elsewhere. It functions as a transitional/bridging statement in the Torah's argument rather than a standalone conceptual node.
